start_room.title: The Intake Prison — Processing Cell
start_room.text:
Cold stone. Fluorescent strips flickering in a cracked ceiling. The smell of antiseptic layered over something older — fear, and whatever they use to process new arrivals.

You come to on a metal bunk. A placard on the wall reads: INTAKE SUBJECT — WORLD-EARTH — 001. Below it, a laminated card explains the competition in bureaucratic language. Ten worlds. Ten-floor gauntlet. Two survive. The rest are processed.

The Overseers built this prison to eliminate the weakest competitors before Floor 2. Some of the other worlds sent representatives who are already in here. Most of them are already gone.

The cell door is open. They do that — give you a running start. It makes the data more interesting.

A rusted utility key sits on the floor just inside the door. Left corridor: boot steps, the scrape of body armor. Guard patrol. Right corridor: the sound of breathing that isn't quite right anymore.

choices.text: Head left — the guard patrol corridor
Head right — the prisoner ward

left_path.title: Guard Patrol Corridor
left_path.text:
The corridor is narrow, lit by strips that hum at irregular intervals. A guard stands at the far end, back to you, watching through a barred viewport into the cell block beyond. Standard armor. Shock baton on the belt. Military posture.

They haven't noticed you yet.

To your left, a section of wall has buckled — a pocket of structural damage where the inner layer has partially caved in. Something pale catches the light inside the crack.

choices.text: Rush the guard before they turn around
Squeeze into the wall crack first

left_crack.title: Structural Damage Pocket
left_crack.text:
The gap is barely a meter deep — a pocket formed when the ceiling shifted and the inner wall cracked. Someone was here before you. A crude message is scratched into the stone in three languages; in yours it reads: 'WARDEN WAS WORLD-4. DOESN'T REMEMBER. DON'T REMIND IT.'

Below that, in different handwriting: 'Phase 2 loses patience. Bait it.'

A sealed kit rests in the rubble — someone stashed it here and didn't come back for it. The wall to the left has an older crack — deeper than this one, and someone has recently pried at the edges of an access panel set flush into the stone.

choices.text: Take the kit and go face the guard
Leave the kit — you travel light
Push the displaced stone behind the main crack — a hollow clicks open
Slip into the filing alcove — the access panel has been pried open recently

left_path_combat.title: Guard Takedown
left_path_combat.text:
The guard turns at the last second — trained reflex, not luck. The shock baton swings up. They've processed a lot of intake subjects. They expect this.

So do you.

right_path.title: Prisoner Ward
right_path.text:
The ward runs long — cells on both sides, most empty. The doors were opened when the competition started. The Overseers don't lock things they don't need locked anymore.

Not all the inmates left. Some of them couldn't.

Whatever the facility did to them during processing — the procedures, the intake assessment, whatever 'capability evaluation' actually means — it changed a few of them. The cell bars in the third block have been bent from the inside. Shapes move in the dim light at the end of the ward, making sounds that are almost words.

Near the ward exit, an overturned supply trolley has spilled sealed medical containers across the floor. To the right, a side door leads into a quieter secondary block.

choices.text: Move through the main ward toward the supply trolley
Take the side door into the secondary block

right_upstream.title: Secondary Cell Block
right_upstream.text:
Quieter here. Lower-risk inmates, according to the signage. The cells are still open but the ward itself is untouched — the mutants in the main block haven't crossed the threshold yet.

One cell at the end has been converted into a rough infirmary by whoever was here before the competition. Labeled containers, basic instruments, a cot with clean linen. The medical kit on the shelf is intact.

A low rhythmic sound carries through the wall from the main ward. Something large, pacing. Near the far end of the block, past the infirmary cell, a maintenance alcove shows signs of recent activity — someone has set up inside it.

choices.text: Take the basic medical kit
Take the larger treatment kit from the cabinet
Grab everything worth grabbing
Check the maintenance alcove at the far end — someone has set up there

right_path_combat.title: Mutant Encounter
right_path_combat.text:
It comes out of the third cell fast — a prisoner the intake process warped beyond recognition. The muscle development is wrong. The eyes don't track right. It moves like something that used to know how to think and is working from memory.

It's not specifically hunting you. It's just hungry, and you're there.

trap_room.title: Secured Access Corridor
trap_room.text:
Beyond the guard post, the corridor is rigged. Tripwire at shin height — nearly invisible. Pressure tiles in the floor, discolored slightly from the surrounding stone. A motion sensor above the far door, amber light blinking.

Old security infrastructure, still functional. The Overseers left it running.

Through the reinforced viewport in the far door: a storeroom. Shelving. Sealed containers. Worth reaching if you can manage it.

A control panel is mounted near the entrance — cracked screen, blinking amber. Guard access terminal.

choices.text: Sprint straight through — take the hits
Move carefully, testing each tile
Work the control panel — reroute the sensors
Use the guard's key on the access terminal — full override

security_lockdown.title: Security Lockdown
security_lockdown.text:
The trap corridor ends in a checkpoint cage. The door behind you slams shut before the one ahead opens. Amber lights switch to red. A ceiling speaker clicks once, then a retired security drone drops from its charging rail.

The prison does not let armed subjects stroll into the junction without one more measurement.

security_records.title: Security Records Office
security_records.text:
Past the checkpoint cage, the corridor opens into a records office. Metal cabinets line the walls. Half the drawers are open, spilling intake files across the floor. The files are not prisoner records. They are performance predictions.

Earth-001 is stamped across one folder. The page inside lists your estimated survival time in minutes.

A second door leads deeper into staff-only territory. The lock has already accepted your presence. The facility wants to keep measuring you.

choices.text: Cross-reference the Warden access logs and move on
Pocket the emergency dressing from a desk drawer

barracks_checkpoint.title: Barracks Checkpoint
barracks_checkpoint.text:
The barracks door opens onto rows of overturned bunks and wall-mounted weapon racks stripped almost clean. Almost.

A staff enforcer steps from behind the last bunk, visor cracked, baton already humming. They are not surprised to see you. The records office warned them before you arrived.

armory_lockup.title: Armory Lockup
armory_lockup.text:
The armory is mostly empty, but the authorization terminal still works. It asks for a living staff signature. The enforcer's cracked visor provides enough biometric residue for the terminal to accept a temporary route authorization.

A drawer clicks open under the console. Inside: a stamped security route token and a short note from someone who tried this path before you. 'Do not go straight to the Warden. Search the junction first.'

choices.text: Take the security route authorization and enter the junction
Search the bottom drawer before leaving

reward_room.title: Confiscated Items Locker
reward_room.text:
The supply trolley is on its side but the sealed containers are intact. The labels are intake manifest codes — everything confiscated from arriving prisoners during processing.

Some of this was taken from the other world-representatives. You can tell by the markings — one container has script you've never seen, from a world the competition has presumably already finished with. Whatever they brought, it's yours now.

The locker on the east wall is still locked, but the hasp is bent.

choices.text: Take the sealed medical container
Take the currency pouch — facility scrip, still spendable
Pry the locker open — something rattles inside
Search the trolley frame — intake manifests sometimes have a secondary compartment

quarantine_lockdown.title: Quarantine Lockdown
quarantine_lockdown.text:
The locker room exit seals before you reach it. White lights flare across the floor in a scanning grid. The warped prisoners in the ward were not the only failed subjects.

A half-processed intake subject pulls itself out of an observation cradle, still dragging restraint cables. Its wrist tag flashes: QUARANTINE BREACH.

ward_observation.title: Observation Theater
ward_observation.text:
Beyond quarantine, the ward becomes clinical. A tiered observation room overlooks a treatment floor below. The glass is cracked from the inside.

Screens still loop archived footage: prisoners waking, screaming, changing, then being tagged as failed assets. One clip shows the service corridor code projected on a monitor before the feed cuts out.

choices.text: Copy the service code fragment and descend to containment
Search the observation desk for supplies

containment_hall.title: Containment Hall
containment_hall.text:
The containment hall is all reinforced glass and emergency foam. Most cells are empty. One is not.

The thing inside was halfway through becoming something useful to the Overseers when the lockdown failed. It throws itself through the cracked door before you can pass.

specimen_records.title: Specimen Records Archive
specimen_records.text:
The records archive is colder than the hall. Specimen files sit in sealed wall slots, each marked by world and viability rating. Earth has no rating yet.

The central terminal offers a ward route authorization in exchange for confirming the containment breach has been neutralized. It is not asking whether you survived. It can see that part.

choices.text: Confirm the breach is neutralized and enter the junction
Open a refrigerated med slot before leaving

merge_room.title: Prison Junction
merge_room.text:
The junction is a wide security hub — monitoring stations on three walls, most screens dark. One is still active, cycling through facility camera feeds: empty corridors, open cells, a top-down view of the ward you came through.

A second screen shows a competition feed. Text scrolls: 'ACTIVE COMPETITORS — FLOOR 1: 3. FLOORS 2+: 4. ELIMINATED: 3.' Then: 'WORLD-EARTH REPRESENTATIVE ADVANCING. RANK: UNCONFIRMED.'

Three side passages lead off the hub. Ahead, a heavy door marked RESTRICTED ACCESS — WARDEN AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED.

You check your condition before going further.

choices.text: Check the guard break room off the left passage
Look in the medical station to the right
Follow the chemical smell from the back passage
Enter the lit maintenance refuge beside the checkpoint
Push through the RESTRICTED ACCESS door with security route authorization
Push through the RESTRICTED ACCESS door with ward route authorization
Use the six-digit service code with your route token
Examine the scored marks on the east wall — a pattern, not damage

warden_trap.title: Guard Break Room
warden_trap.text:
A staff room — lockers, a table with cold rations, a duty roster on the wall. The last shift entry is dated the day the competition started. No entries after.

One locker hangs open. Another is padlocked. On the table: a forgotten personal kit, small, zipped.

The floor near the padlocked locker has the faint outline of pressure sensors — maintenance grade. Obvious if you know what to look for. A secondary door at the back, marked SUB-LEVEL ACCESS, stands slightly ajar — cold air rises from below.

choices.text: Search the open locker — reach carefully
Force the padlocked locker — step over the sensor plates
Take the kit from the table
Pull the shift captain's clearance tab from the duty terminal
Leave the break room
Take the sub-level stairs — check what's below

supply_cache.title: Medical Station
supply_cache.text:
Institutional white walls gone yellow. Cabinets bolted shut, most locks broken. Someone moved through here quickly and took the obvious things. What's left is still useful.

A treatment log on the cot has been filled out for intake subject W-7-031. The handwriting gets shakier toward the end. The notes stop mid-procedure.

The supply room behind the partition is sealed but the door lock is stripped.

choices.text: Search the remaining cabinets
Force the supply room — stripped lock won't hold
Leave the station

alchemy_lab.title: Contraband Stash
alchemy_lab.text:
The chemical smell comes from a cavity behind a false wall panel — a stash someone built over time, slowly, probably during intake processing when the guards weren't watching. Improvised equipment. Two sealed vials.

One labeled CLEAN in block letters. One with no label, amber-colored, faintly warm through the glass.

The Overseers' sensors don't cover this corner. You checked.

choices.text: Drink the CLEAN vial
Drink the unlabeled amber vial
Check the false panel edge — a second cavity inside the first
Leave without touching anything

hall_return.title: Back to the Junction
hall_return.text: You retrace your steps to the security hub. The competition feed is still scrolling on the active monitor. The RESTRICTED ACCESS door ahead hasn't moved. Three competitors still active on this floor — you, and two others you haven't seen yet.

choices.text: Return to the junction

maintenance_refuge.title: Maintenance Refuge
maintenance_refuge.text:
A maintenance alcove has been converted into a tiny refuge: cot, sealed water, a half-working terminal, and a hand-painted line across the threshold. SAFE WHILE LIGHT IS GREEN.

The light is green. For now.

Someone used this place to watch the checkpoint door. Notes on the wall explain that the Warden route needs two separate authorizations: staff security clearance and a maintenance override. Bravery does not open Overseer locks.

choices.text: Rest on the cot for a few minutes
Pull the maintenance override from the wall terminal
Read the warning notes about the Warden door
Return to the junction

secret_room.title: Hidden Cell Block
secret_room.text:
The marks aren't random. It takes a moment to resolve — a hand-width pattern pressed into the stone at regular intervals, forming a frame around a section of wall. You push. The panel swings inward on dry hinges.

A cell beyond, converted into a living space. Neat, organized, occupied for a while. On the wall: a full schematic of the facility's upper block, annotated carefully. A note in the margin reads: 'Warden has two states. Patient and not. The second one is faster but it burns out. Wait it out if you can.'

The desk holds a personal log. The last entry: 'Day 14. World-4 still running. Getting harder to think clearly. The intake process leaves residue.' It stops there.

A cache is tucked under the cot. Whoever lived here either made it out or didn't need it anymore. Behind the filing cabinet, the stone doesn't sit quite right — a seam runs where there shouldn't be one.

choices.text: Take the medical supplies from the cache
Study the combat schematic — learn the Warden's pattern
Take the currency bundle from the desk
Pick up the focus ring on the windowsill
Move the filing cabinet — trace the seam in the stone behind it
Seal the panel and return to the junction

peril_room.title: Security Lockdown Corridor
peril_room.text:
The RESTRICTED door seals behind you with a magnetic click. Overhead lights shift to red. A recorded voice begins: 'Unauthorized access detected. Initiating lockdown protocol.'

Heavy security grates begin descending from the ceiling on both ends of the corridor — slow but inevitable. Between them: a checkpoint door with a keypad. On the floor near the far grate, a sealed supply container sits where someone dropped it in a hurry.

The grates have maybe thirty seconds before they're fully down. To the side, barely visible in the red light, is a second door — flush with the wall, no signage, a recessed keypad with a six-digit input panel.

choices.text: Present both Warden authorizations at the checkpoint
Slide under the far grate and grab the container
Use the staff clearance on the keypad — authorized override
Brace both grates simultaneously — hold them open long enough
Enter the six-digit code on the recessed panel — access the service corridor
Retreat to the junction and search for authorizations

deadly_room.title: Processing Checkpoint
deadly_room.text:
A staging area beyond the lockdown corridor — wide, built for processing large numbers at once. Strip lighting. Drain channels in the floor. You don't want to think about what for.

Not empty.

A senior enforcer waits at the far end. Larger than the intake guards, armor reinforced at the joints, carrying a shock baton that hums with active charge. They've been watching your progress on the monitors.

'End of the line, Earth-001.' They know your designation. Of course they do. Everything in this facility is logged.

boss_room.title: The Warden's Office
boss_room.text:
A wide corridor beyond the checkpoint leads to double doors — institutional metal, recently cleaned. A plaque reads: FACILITY DIRECTOR.

The Warden.

You know the designation from the competition feed, but the details are classified. Former world-representative. Former competitor. Placed well enough in a previous cycle to survive, but not well enough to go free — so the Overseers kept them and put them to work. That's what rank 3 or 4 gets you. That's what you're trying to avoid.

The doors open before you touch them.

Inside: the furniture has been cleared to the walls, leaving an open floor. The Warden stands at the center. Tall. Composed. They're wearing their world's combat equipment under a layer of Overseer-installed control hardware — slim collar, two bracelet nodes, a cortical sensor at the temple.

They look at you for a moment. Then: 'You made it further than most do on the first floor.' A pause that feels like a calculation. 'That ends here.'

combat.name: The Warden
combat.intro: The Warden does not rush. They advance with the patience of someone who has ended this same fight many times before. The control hardware on their body pulses at a steady interval.
combat.victoryText:
The composure breaks before the body does. A sound that might be surprise — or recognition. The Warden drops to one knee. The control hardware goes dark: collar, bracelet nodes, all of it.

They look up. The eyes are clearer now without the Overseers' systems running. 'World... Four...' Then nothing. They settle to the floor.

The competition continues. The Warden will not be sending any more performance reports.

phases.intro: The control hardware flickers — then goes to emergency override. Whatever protocol the Overseers installed to keep the Warden compliant just failed. The person underneath, the one who was a competitor once and lost, comes through all at once. The movement changes completely. This is not patience. This is rage that has been waiting a very long time.

end_room.title: Floor Clear — Ascending
end_room.text:
The service elevator at the far end of the facility's upper level responds to your clearance — combat authorization from defeating the Warden, or administrative authorization from the Overseer's evaluation. The lock reads either the same way.

You step in. The doors close.

The Overseers' signal cuts through almost immediately, neutral and precise: 'World-Earth representative. Floor 1 performance logged. Method noted. Advancing to Floor 2.'

A pause that feels longer than it should — then: 'Current field: 6 active competitors across all floors. Earth rank: unconfirmed. Competition continues.'

The elevator rises. The intake prison drops away. Whatever is on Floor 2, it is not a prison. The Overseers built this place to filter the weak. You are not that.

Not yet.

choices.text: Step into Floor 2. [FLOOR 1 COMPLETE]

lore_room.title: Prisoner Processing Records
lore_room.text:
A cramped supply alcove behind the crack in the wall, invisible unless you're looking for it. Filing cabinets line three walls — most drawers welded shut or locked, but one is wedged open with a bent piece of rebar.

Inside: intake forms. Competitor profiles from the current cycle and at least two previous ones. Evaluation logs annotated in three different writing systems. The administrative machinery of a dungeon that predates your world's entry into the competition by decades.

One file is thicker than the others. The name is blacked out in red, but the designation is visible: FLOOR 1 OVERSEER — INTAKE DIVISION. The attached performance log is mostly neutral. The final entry is not: 'Subject continues to withhold evaluation protocol disclosure from challengers despite standing requirement. Third notice filed. No corrective action taken. Recommend continued monitoring.'

Stapled to the file, on an adhesive strip: a six-digit access code.

You recognize the format — service corridor authorization. Somewhere in this facility, there is a door this code opens. The Overseers know challengers could find it. They haven't removed it.

choices.text: Copy the access code — this could open something
Read the competitor profiles — study the ones who came before you
Leave the records room

merchant_room.title: Salvage Trader's Alcove
merchant_room.text:
A World 6 competitor has set up in the maintenance alcove at the end of the secondary block. Former active entrant — delisted after a draw in a previous cycle and reassigned as a neutral observer with limited trading privileges. They've been in this dungeon for two seasons. It shows.

They look up when you enter. 'Earth. Current cycle.' Not hostile. Not warm.

A folding case is open between them. Items arranged with the precision of someone who has survived a long time by being very careful about everything. They sell. They don't fight. The Overseers consider them useful infrastructure.

'You're the first one to make it this far in your cycle,' they say. 'The others didn't check the side block.'

choices.text: Buy a Small Potion (15 gold)
Buy an Antidote (10 gold)
Buy a Training Sword (25 gold)
Buy a Guard Vest (30 gold)
Ask about the floor's layout — what's ahead
Ask about the previous challengers on this floor
Ask what this place is and what has to be done
Ask how the Warden door opens
Investigate the other competitor at the back of the alcove — you're not alone here
Leave the alcove

rival_room.title: Ward Corridor — Rival Encounter
rival_room.text:
Coming around the alcove's inner corridor, you nearly walk into them.

World 3 representative. Fast — already in a combat stance before you've fully processed what you're looking at. The competition ID is etched into their equipment: TARION / W3-047 / ACTIVE. They've been here longer than you. Their gear shows it.

'Earth.' They say your world like it's a category. Not hostile. Not friendly. A flat assessment.

'Same floor.' A pause. 'Same checkpoint coming up. Only one authorized passage per competitor.'

They don't give you time to respond. Competition logic: if you're here, you're in the way.

dead_end_passage.title: Sub-Level — Detention Corridor
dead_end_passage.text:
The stairs descend into a lower corridor — older than the main facility, stone rather than processed material. The air is cold and stagnant. Emergency lighting only, half the strips dark.

At the far end: a sentry. Not standard prison staff — older hardware, a security model the facility retired at least a decade ago. It's still running on its original protocols. It has no context for the competition, no concept of the Overseers. It just knows unauthorized access when it detects it.

The corridor dead-ends behind it. Whatever this section was built for, it's not used anymore.

dead_end_loot.title: Sub-Level — Detention Vault
dead_end_loot.text:
With the sentry down, the corridor end resolves: a single detention cell, long-term, occupied for an extended period and recently vacated. The person who lived here either left when the competition started or was moved.

The cell is stripped of most personal effects, but they didn't get everything. Wall messages scratched over weeks or months — a count of days, names of other competitors, fragments of notation in a script you can't read. One message is in your language: 'If you found this, you went deeper than most. That's something. Use it.'

Under the thin mattress, something wrapped in cloth.

choices.text: Search the mattress — unwrap what's hidden there
Read the wall messages carefully — trace the full count of days
Head back up to the break room

overseer_antechamber.title: Service Wing — Restricted Access
overseer_antechamber.text:
The code works. The door opens — or if you found the hidden passage from the secret cell block, you step through into the same space from a different direction.

The service wing is different from everything else in this facility. Carpeted floor, worn flat but still there. Climate-controlled air that actually functions. The hum of processing equipment from behind a wall, regular and unhurried.

A sign: FLOOR 1 INTAKE OVERSIGHT — AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY.

Below it, handwritten on a laminated card: Evaluation requests acknowledged during active competition windows. Current window: OPEN.

The door at the end of the corridor is unlocked. Someone has been expecting challengers to reach this point. Or they've been hoping they wouldn't.

choices.text: Proceed to the Overseer's office
Turn back to the checkpoint corridor

overseer_chamber.title: The Overseer's Station
overseer_chamber.text:
The office is orderly. Systematically maintained in a way that suggests either deep discipline or something very close to obsession.

The Overseer sits behind a workstation built for monitoring intake assessments — a dozen screens showing facility feeds, competitor tracking data, performance logs. They're smaller than you expected, and older. No collar, no bracelet nodes, no combat hardware of any kind. Administrative uniform, recently pressed.

They look up when you enter. They don't reach for anything.

'World-Earth representative.' Their voice is level. 'You found the service corridor. Most don't.'

A pause while they pull up a file on the terminal. Your file.

'Under competition protocol, article 7, section B — any challenger who reaches a floor's overseer station before the primary combat clearance may request formal evaluation as an alternative completion method. Most Overseers don't inform challengers of this. I am required to honor requests.'

Another pause.

'The evaluation is not easy. And it does not spare you from what comes after Floor 1.'

choices.text: Invoke Evaluation Protocol 7-B — cite the access code from the records
Request a formal evaluation — proceed through the standard assessment
Ask what happened to the previous challengers who reached this floor
Ask what the Overseer actually knows about the competition — and Earth's position
Turn back — reconsider the combat route

evaluation_argument.title: The Evaluation — Formal Assessment
evaluation_argument.text:
The Overseer activates a secondary terminal. Three assessment criteria appear on the display: adaptive reasoning under pressure, resource management across uncertain conditions, and systemic compliance awareness.

'These are the standard completion metrics for Floor 1,' they say. 'You have been evaluated against them since you entered the facility. This is the formal request for the results to count toward floor completion rather than raw combat performance.'

They wait. They've done this before — or they haven't, and this is the first time anyone has made it this far. You can't tell which.

'Address the criteria. Or don't. The choice is yours, and it is the last one you make on this floor either way.'

choices.text: Present the documentation from the intake records — the criteria are written in the protocol
Argue the case: reaching this point demonstrates all three criteria more completely than combat would
Accept the evaluation criteria without contestation — answer honestly what you can
Challenge the Overseer's authority — this protocol was never disclosed to challengers
Turn back and reconsider

floor2_safe_room.title: Floor 2 - Transit Safe Room
floor2_safe_room.text: The elevator opens into a room that feels deliberately untouched. Clean cot. Working sink. A trader waits behind a reinforced counter, sorting inventory without looking up. Three sealed doors line the far wall: red, blue, and black. The lock panel beside them has one warning: EXIT SELECTION FINAL.

choices.text: Rest on the bed before choosing a door
Buy Large Potion - 30 gold
Buy Phase Edge - 80 gold
Buy Mesh Armor - 85 gold
Buy Calibrated Lens - 50 gold
Leave through the red door
Leave through the blue door
Leave through the black door

floor2_red_door.title: Floor 2 - Red Door
floor2_red_door.text: The red door seals behind you with a pressure lock. Heat rolls through the corridor ahead, carrying the smell of scorched dust and machine oil. This route does not charge at you. It waits, full of old systems that can still be used by someone patient enough to read them.

choices.text: Advance into the pressure gallery

floor2_pressure_gallery.title: Floor 2 - Pressure Gallery
floor2_pressure_gallery.text: A long gallery stretches ahead, its floor divided into metal plates. Some sit a fraction lower than the others. The wall monitors still work, but every display shows a different pressure reading. Someone crossed here recently and marked a narrow route in chalk. Someone else crossed after them and scratched half the marks away.

choices.text: Follow the remaining chalk marks toward the checkpoint
Search the side maintenance locker
Cross directly through the unstable plates

floor2_broken_checkpoint.title: Floor 2 - Broken Checkpoint
floor2_broken_checkpoint.text: The checkpoint booth has been torn open from the inside. A security scanner sweeps the corridor in a lazy red arc, too damaged to identify you but not damaged enough to ignore. Above the booth, an observation hatch hangs open.

choices.text: Time the damaged scanner and slip through
Climb into the observation hatch
Force the scanner to cycle early

floor2_observation_nest.title: Floor 2 - Observation Nest
floor2_observation_nest.text: The hatch opens into a cramped watcher station above the checkpoint. Dusty screens show fragments of the three lanes: red systems, blue attrition corridors, black geometry that refuses to hold still, and the boss chamber where they all converge. A notebook rests beside the console, written in a competitor's scouting shorthand.

choices.text: Study the notebook and take the emergency vial
Copy the rival's scout map from the screens
Return to the checkpoint below

floor2_supply_fault.title: Floor 2 - Supply Fault
floor2_supply_fault.text: The maintenance locker is larger inside than it looked from the gallery. A supply lift sits jammed halfway between floors, spilling med-cases and sealed ration bricks into a mesh cage. The lift motor keeps trying to correct itself with a grinding whine.

choices.text: Pull the reachable med-case from the cage
Force the jammed lift for the lower crate
Use the service door beyond the locker
Return to the pressure gallery

floor2_service_crawl.title: Floor 2 - Service Crawl
floor2_service_crawl.text: The forward route narrows into a service crawlspace lined with hot conduit. Loose tags hang from the pipes, each one stamped with a different world's symbol. The crawl forks around a locked equipment niche before dropping into the conduit split.

choices.text: Drop down into the conduit split
Pry open the rival-marked equipment niche
Crawl through the hot conduit without slowing

floor2_rival_cache.title: Floor 2 - Rival Cache
floor2_rival_cache.text: The niche opens into a hidden cache marked with World-3's angular script. Whoever left it expected to come back after scouting the boss route. They did not. Inside: a field note about the shared boss, route colors, and a carefully wrapped piece of equipment.

choices.text: Take the wrapped armor plate
Read the field note and leave it for later
Strip the cache's emergency gold foil
Return to the service crawl

floor2_split_conduit.title: Floor 2 - Split Conduit
floor2_split_conduit.text: Two routes continue from the conduit junction. One slopes down into a maintenance bypass where the air is breathable but the footing is bad. The other cuts straight through a sparking transformer corridor, faster and nastier.

choices.text: Take the lower maintenance bypass
Cut through the sparking transformer corridor

floor2_gatehouse.title: Floor 2 - Gatehouse
floor2_gatehouse.text: The lane's systems finally stop pretending to be passive. A gatehouse blocks the final corridor, its shutters half-closed and its defense unit awake behind them. It has been listening to every plate, hatch, and conduit you touched.

floor2_boss_antechamber.title: Floor 2 - Boss Antechamber
floor2_boss_antechamber.text: Beyond the gatehouse, the red lane ends in a circular antechamber. Blue and black door symbols are carved into two sealed side arches, proof that the other routes arrive here too. Ahead, the shared boss door breathes light through its seams.

choices.text: Check the emergency cabinet before the boss
Open the shared boss door

floor2_blue_door.title: Floor 2 - Blue Door
floor2_blue_door.text: The blue door closes with a soft pneumatic sigh. The corridor beyond is quiet, washed in cold light. Water runs somewhere under the floor grating, and every few steps the tiles click like they are counting your weight. There are no side passages here. Only the line.

choices.text: Enter the gauntlet lock

floor2_gauntlet_lock.title: Floor 2 - Gauntlet Lock
floor2_gauntlet_lock.text: The first chamber is a lock box. The blue door behind you seals, then a second door ahead begins counting down from ten. The room offers no route choice, only preparation time and the certainty that the gauntlet has noticed you.

choices.text: Brace as the second door opens

floor2_first_crush.title: Floor 2 - First Crush
floor2_first_crush.text: A compression gate slams down behind you and a heavy frame unfolds from the ceiling. The gauntlet opens with weight, pressure, and a machine built to make backing up impossible.

floor2_bleeder_hall.title: Floor 2 - Bleeder Hall
floor2_bleeder_hall.text: The hall after the crush frame is lined with needle vents. They hiss in sequence, not enough to kill, enough to take something from you before the next fight. The floor drains are old and red-brown.

choices.text: Move through the needle pattern

floor2_sentry_line.title: Floor 2 - Sentry Line
floor2_sentry_line.text: Three sentry pylons rotate into alignment down the corridor. They fire in disciplined volleys, forcing you forward between bursts. This lane is not testing cleverness. It is counting endurance.

floor2_no_rest_crossing.title: Floor 2 - No-Rest Crossing
floor2_no_rest_crossing.text: A bench waits in the middle of the crossing. The word REST is painted above it in clean white letters. The floor around it is scorched by old impact marks. The joke is not subtle.

choices.text: Ignore the bench and keep moving
Grab the ration pack under the bench without sitting

floor2_double_bind.title: Floor 2 - Double Bind
floor2_double_bind.text: The next door opens into a narrow chamber with two restraint rigs hanging from rails. They move like predators, one trying to pin your guard, the other trying to punish the opening.

floor2_killbox.title: Floor 2 - Killbox
floor2_killbox.text: The corridor widens into a square chamber with shutters on every wall. They open one by one, releasing a defense pattern that gives you no cover and no time to breathe.

floor2_last_meter.title: Floor 2 - Last Meter
floor2_last_meter.text: The last corridor is short enough to see the end. That makes it worse. Each step triggers a different pressure hammer from the walls, turning the final stretch into a tax paid in bruises.

choices.text: Cross the last meter under the hammers

floor2_gauntlet_antechamber.title: Floor 2 - Gauntlet Antechamber
floor2_gauntlet_antechamber.text: The blue lane finally releases you into an antechamber facing the same boss seal as the other routes. No caches. No clever detours. Just a record of how much you still have left.

choices.text: Step through to the shared boss

floor2_black_door.title: Floor 2 - Black Door
floor2_black_door.text: The black door does not open so much as stop being there. Past it, the hallway is too wide for the space the safe room occupied. The walls carry old markings from worlds that were not supposed to leave records behind. This lane does not raise weapons. It asks questions.

choices.text: Step into the cipher threshold

floor2_cipher_threshold.title: Floor 2 - Cipher Threshold
floor2_cipher_threshold.text: A sealed arch waits under three rotating glyphs. Each glyph repeats a number in a different base. The trick is not translation; it is noticing that all three describe the same count.

choices.text: Align the glyphs to the shared count
Force the arch to accept a rough match

floor2_mirror_grid.title: Floor 2 - Mirror Grid
floor2_mirror_grid.text: Mirrors hang over a grid of black tiles. The reflected route is wrong in the ordinary way and right in the important one: every safe step appears one tile behind where your eyes expect it.

choices.text: Walk the reflected route, not the visible one
Trust the floor markings instead of the mirrors

floor2_weight_riddle.title: Floor 2 - Weight Riddle
floor2_weight_riddle.text: Four plinths rise from the floor. One asks for what you carried in, one for what you lost, one for what you learned, and one for what you refuse to give. Only one is physical.

choices.text: Place a ration wrapper on the physical plinth and leave the rest empty
Load all four plinths with loose debris

floor2_tone_lock.title: Floor 2 - Tone Lock
floor2_tone_lock.text: A door hums in five tones. Four are steady. One tone wavers every time you move. The lock is listening for the sound the room makes when you stop trying to hurry.

choices.text: Wait through the full tone cycle before touching the panel
Match the loudest tone immediately

floor2_memory_walk.title: Floor 2 - Memory Walk
floor2_memory_walk.text: The corridor shows three versions of the room behind you. One is exact, one is flattering, and one includes the mistake you almost made. The exit opens only for the memory that admits the error.

choices.text: Choose the memory with the almost-mistake
Choose the perfect version of the room

floor2_logic_well.title: Floor 2 - Logic Well
floor2_logic_well.text: A deep circular shaft divides the lane. Three statements burn above it: one true, one false, one useful. The bridge forms under the useful one, because the Overseers care less about truth than function.

choices.text: Stand beneath the useful statement
Stand beneath the true statement

floor2_symbol_bridge.title: Floor 2 - Symbol Bridge
floor2_symbol_bridge.text: A bridge of symbols assembles in midair, one piece at a time. Some symbols mean weight. Some mean direction. One means survivor, but only when it is upside down.

choices.text: Step on the inverted survivor symbol
Step on the upright survivor symbol

floor2_final_proof.title: Floor 2 - Final Proof
floor2_final_proof.text: The final puzzle offers no symbols at all. Just a blank panel and a countdown. The proof is not an answer. It is whether you trust the pattern enough to do nothing.

choices.text: Let the countdown expire without touching the panel
Press the panel before the countdown ends

floor2_puzzle_antechamber.title: Floor 2 - Puzzle Antechamber
floor2_puzzle_antechamber.text: The black lane ends in a quiet antechamber with no enemies, no traps, and no reward chest. The reward was understanding the floor before it tried to kill you. The shared boss door waits ahead.

choices.text: Carry the solved pattern into the shared boss chamber

floor2_shared_boss.title: Floor 2 - Shared Boss
floor2_shared_boss.text: The three Floor 2 lanes converge in a chamber built around a suspended engine core. The boss waits beneath it, shaped by whichever path brought you here but loyal to none of them. Red heat, blue pressure, and black puzzle-light pulse through its armor in sequence.

combat.name: Convergence Warden
combat.intro: The suspended engine core opens like an eye. The Convergence Warden drops beneath it, armor lit by three route colors. It does not choose a lane. It chooses all of them.
combat.victoryText:
The Convergence Warden tries to cycle one more protocol, but the three colors desync. Red heat vents into the floor. Blue pressure cracks the chamber wall. Black puzzle-light resolves into a single answer: survived.

The engine core folds inward and leaves a dense relic behind. Floor 2 has no more routes to test you with.

advantages.message: The tactical readout exposes the Red Protocol's timing.
The solved pattern strips the Black Protocol's sweep sequence.

phases.intro: The red heat gutters out. Blue pressure floods the armor, turning the fight into a compressed gauntlet with no space to breathe.
The chamber lights cut to black. Symbols bloom across the Warden's plating, each attack arriving one beat before the obvious answer.

floor2_clear_room.title: Floor 2 Clear - Descent Lock
floor2_clear_room.text:
The Convergence Warden collapses into three fading colors. Red systems vent heat into the walls. Blue pressure doors unlock one after another. Black puzzle-light resolves into a straight line pointing down.

An elevator rises from beneath the boss chamber, but it does not open like the safe room doors did. A panel reads: FLOOR 2 PERFORMANCE LOGGED. FLOOR 3 ACCESS PREPARED.

The Overseers' voice follows a beat later: 'World-Earth representative. Floor 2 clear. Route variance recorded. Convergence response survived.'

The elevator doors part onto darkness and deeper machinery. Floor 3 is below you. The competition continues.

choices.text: Step into the elevator toward Floor 3. [FLOOR 2 COMPLETE]

floor3_market.title: Floor 3 - Contract Market
floor3_market.text:
Floor 3 opens into a market built inside an impossible station. Venders call from stalls made of salvaged dungeon metal while contract brokers sit beneath hanging portal frames, each one selling risk with a smile and a stamped receipt.

Mara Voss keeps the red hunt desk with trophy tags pinned to her coat. Tallow Jin sells bottles from a furnace-warm medicine cart. Sister Quen repairs armor under a cracked sanctuary bell, and Nix Ledger runs odds from a booth of clicking brass counters.

Contract Board: 0/5 stamped. Hunt and Recovery are open. Puzzle unlocks at 1/5, Escort at 2/5, Debt at 3/5, and the Boss portal at 5/5. The air is safe by rule, not kindness. Weapons are lowered. Prices are high. Every contract portal hums with a different color.

choices.text: Visit Tallow Jin - buy a Large Potion (40 gold)
Visit Tallow Jin - buy an Antidote (18 gold)
Visit Mara Voss - buy a Market Spike (95 gold)
Visit Sister Quen - buy Contract Lamellar (100 gold)
Visit Nix Ledger - buy a Broker Abacus (80 gold)
Visit Nix Ledger - buy the Arbiter Clause relic (120 gold)
Ask Nix Ledger about contract portals
Hear Mara Voss call your first mark good enough to risk better work
Hear Sister Quen warn the market is starting to bet on you
Hear Nix Ledger quote the Arbiter's odds after five contracts
Accept the Hunt Contract portal
Accept the Recovery Contract portal
Accept the Puzzle Contract portal
Accept the Escort Contract portal
Accept the Debt Contract portal
Enter the boss portal after completing five contracts

floor3_hunt_portal.title: Floor 3 - Hunt Portal
floor3_hunt_portal.text: The hunt broker stamps your wrist with a red sigil. The portal opens onto a room that smells like hot iron and old trophies.

choices.text: Step through to hunt the marked target
Return to the market

floor3_hunt_trace.title: Contract - Hunt Trace
floor3_hunt_trace.text: The trophy room is empty except for heat-scratches across the floor and fresh iron filings in the corners. The beast is circling the room behind the room.

choices.text: Study the spoor before forcing the second door
Kick the second door open before it finishes circling

floor3_hunt_room.title: Contract - Hunt
floor3_hunt_room.text: A brass hunting floor unfolds under your feet. The target waits in the center, all plated shoulders and contract tags hammered into its hide.

floor3_hunt_complete.title: Contract Complete - Hunt
floor3_hunt_complete.text: The hunt sigil burns cold, then turns into a stamped mark. A Hunt Seal forms under it, red-edged and sharp enough to make the Arbiter's future ledger bleed. Somewhere in the market, Mara Voss updates your tally.

choices.text: Claim the Hunt Contract mark and return

floor3_recovery_portal.title: Floor 3 - Recovery Portal
floor3_recovery_portal.text: The recovery broker slides a claim slip under the portal frame. 'Bring back the sealed case. Do not open the sealed case. Everyone opens the sealed case.'

choices.text: Enter the recovery portal
Return to the market

floor3_recovery_vault.title: Contract - Recovery Vault
floor3_recovery_vault.text: The first vault door is already open. That is the trap. Two claim tags hang from the handle, one legal and one forged.

choices.text: Compare the claim tags before touching the lock
Tear off both tags and take the risk

floor3_recovery_room.title: Contract - Recovery
floor3_recovery_room.text: The portal drops you into a vault aisle where every lock is already open except the one you need. The sealed case sits behind a trap mesh that tightens whenever you breathe too fast.

choices.text: Lift the sealed case slowly through the mesh
Rip the case free before the mesh closes

floor3_recovery_complete.title: Contract Complete - Recovery
floor3_recovery_complete.text: The sealed case vanishes from your hands and reappears on a broker's desk in the market. A Recovery Seal replaces it, stamped with proof the Arbiter cannot claim every asset on the floor.

choices.text: Claim the Recovery Contract mark and return

floor3_puzzle_portal.title: Floor 3 - Puzzle Portal
floor3_puzzle_portal.text: The puzzle broker says nothing. They only point to a portal filled with stacked receipts, each one folded into a different answer.

choices.text: Enter the puzzle portal
Return to the market

floor3_puzzle_audit.title: Contract - Puzzle Audit
floor3_puzzle_audit.text: Receipts drift like paper birds. Four are lies, one is a duplicate, and the room waits to see whether you count money or motive.

choices.text: Sort the receipts by signature pressure
Sort them by the largest number first

floor3_puzzle_room.title: Contract - Puzzle
floor3_puzzle_room.text: A contract ledger hangs open in midair. Five debts, five names, five impossible totals. The answer is not who owes the most. It is who paid twice.

choices.text: Mark the repeated payer and balance the ledger
Erase the largest debt

floor3_puzzle_complete.title: Contract Complete - Puzzle
floor3_puzzle_complete.text: The ledger closes itself and prints your answer onto a Puzzle Seal. The mark hums with balanced columns, ready to cancel one of the Arbiter's nastier clauses.

choices.text: Claim the Puzzle Contract mark and return

floor3_escort_portal.title: Floor 3 - Escort Portal
floor3_escort_portal.text: The escort broker gestures to a flickering maintenance drone. 'Keep it functioning until the contract site verifies delivery.' The drone looks already offended by reality.

choices.text: Escort the drone through the portal
Return to the market

floor3_escort_route.title: Contract - Escort Route
floor3_escort_route.text: The drone projects two delivery routes. One is longer and lit. One is shorter and full of claw marks. It recommends the claw marks with corporate confidence.

choices.text: Recalibrate the drone and take the longer lit route
Take the claw-mark shortcut before the route changes

floor3_escort_room.title: Contract - Escort
floor3_escort_room.text: The drone rolls into a service corridor and immediately attracts two hostile pylons. It emits one sad confirmation tone and hides behind you.

floor3_escort_complete.title: Contract Complete - Escort
floor3_escort_complete.text: The drone reaches its delivery square and prints your Escort Seal with insulting slowness. Its route data remains inside the mark, waiting to misdirect the Arbiter's orders.

choices.text: Claim the Escort Contract mark and return

floor3_debt_portal.title: Floor 3 - Debt Portal
floor3_debt_portal.text: The debt broker smiles like a closed knife. 'This one is simple. Someone owes the market. Make the books stop noticing.'

choices.text: Enter the debt portal
Return to the market

floor3_debt_counterparty.title: Contract - Debt Counterparty
floor3_debt_counterparty.text: The debtor is gone, but their excuses remain as recorded holograms. Each one contradicts the last by exactly one useful detail.

choices.text: Interview the recordings until the contradiction appears
Break the witness terminal and pocket the emergency scrip

floor3_debt_room.title: Contract - Debt
floor3_debt_room.text: A stall appears without a seller. Scales hang over a contract slate. The slate lists three acceptable payments: gold, blood, or leverage.

choices.text: Pay the debt cleanly (30 gold)
Pay in blood and keep your gold
Find leverage in the fine print

floor3_debt_complete.title: Contract Complete - Debt
floor3_debt_complete.text: The slate zeroes out, then stamps your Debt Seal with a sound like a judge's gavel. The market recognizes paid debt, and that recognition has weight.

choices.text: Claim the Debt Contract mark and return

floor3_boss_portal.title: Floor 3 - Boss Portal
floor3_boss_portal.text: Five contract marks and five seals rise from your inventory and slot themselves into the portal frame. The market quiets. Even the venders stop pretending not to watch. A counter flips from 5/5 to PORTAL LIVE.

choices.text: Enter the boss portal
Return to the market

floor3_boss.title: Floor 3 - The Market Arbiter
floor3_boss.text: The boss chamber is a counting house with no walls. Receipts orbit a central throne. The Market Arbiter looks up from a ledger that already has your name written five times.

combat.name: The Market Arbiter
combat.intro: The Arbiter opens the ledger. Every completed contract becomes a weaponized line item.
combat.victoryText: The ledger splits down the spine. The Arbiter tries to total your debt one last time, but the number resolves to zero.

advantages.message: Mara's Hunt Seal marks the Arbiter's real body among the receipt doubles.
The Recovery Seal proves which assets the Arbiter can no longer claim.
The Puzzle Seal balances the audit before the armor-break clause resolves.
The Escort Seal forces the market pylons to misroute the Arbiter's strongest orders.
The Debt Seal zeroes a line item the Arbiter planned to weaponize.

phases.intro: The market calls in every debt at once.

floor3_clear_room.title: Floor 3 Clear - Market Closed
floor3_clear_room.text:
The market returns all at once: venders shouting, brokers laughing, portals cooling to dull glass. A bell rings five times for the contracts, then once more for the boss.

Mara Voss tips two fingers from the hunt desk. Tallow Jin stops haggling long enough to raise a bottle. Sister Quen folds a strip of contract metal into a quiet blessing. Nix Ledger tears your losing slip in half and writes a new line underneath: SPONSORS WATCHING.

Behind the Arbiter's broken ledger, a black-market elevator opens on a shaft of colder light. The sign above it reads: FLOOR 4 ACCESS PENDING. Whatever waits below has already bought your name from the market.

choices.text: Step toward Floor 4. [FLOOR 3 COMPLETE]

game_over.title: DEFEAT
game_over.text:
The floor rushes up. Vision dims to grey, then black.

The Overseers' system logs the result. Earth's ranking drops. Somewhere in the competition feed, the active competitor count decrements by one.

...but the competition is not the only thing tracking your performance.

choices.text: Accept your fate. [END]

the_end.title: Floor Complete
the_end.text: The Overseers log your progress. Earth holds its position in the rankings — for now.

floor4_elevator.title: Floor 4 - Sponsor Relay
floor4_elevator.text:
The black-market elevator opens into a private relay chamber. No guards. No crowd. Just a vendor in a silver mask, a wall of sponsor logos, and three vault doors waiting for bids. The relay NPC calls themself Vale and speaks like every word has been paid for in advance.

Sponsor Vault rules: collect Vault Keys 0/3. Gold, Blood, and Signal wings each hold one key. Sponsor Pressure offers better rewards if you accept pain, exposure, or a rigged room. The boss gate will not open until all three keys are slotted.

choices.text: Rest in the relay cot before taking a sponsor door
Buy Large Potion - 45 gold
Buy Antidote - 20 gold
Enter the Gold Wing
Enter the Blood Wing
Enter the Signal Wing
Approach the sealed boss gate

floor4_gold_entry.title: Floor 4 - Gold Wing Entrance
floor4_gold_entry.text: The Gold Wing is a silent auction hall. Every door shows a price before it shows a handle. Sponsor drones watch your hands, your inventory, and every flicker of hesitation.

choices.text: Follow the auction lights deeper
Return to the sponsor relay

floor4_gold_auction.title: Floor 4 - Auction Trap
floor4_gold_auction.text: Sponsor Pressure: a contract scroll offers to mark your habits for the watching bidders. The payout is immediate. So is the cost. Refuse, and the room still lets you pass, but the Champion keeps its private data.

choices.text: Accept Sponsor Pressure - sell your combat pattern for gold and a boss counter
Refuse the contract and take the clean route

floor4_gold_vault.title: Floor 4 - Gold Vault
floor4_gold_vault.text: The vault opens onto stacked coin-light and a key suspended inside a glass of liquid gold. A sponsor logo burns away as you touch it.

choices.text: Claim the Gold Vault Key
Leave the emptied Gold Vault

floor4_blood_entry.title: Floor 4 - Blood Wing Entrance
floor4_blood_entry.text: The Blood Wing is a training arena built for spectators who cannot smell the room. Red seats rise into darkness. A rival-branded execution dummy turns its head when you enter.

floor4_blood_trial.title: Floor 4 - Blood Trial
floor4_blood_trial.text: Sponsor Pressure: the floor asks for a signed Blood Writ. Accept, and the Champion loses one of its crowd-funded attack routines. Decline, and you keep your blood but not the advantage.

choices.text: Accept Sponsor Pressure - sign the Blood Writ
Decline the writ and conserve strength

floor4_blood_vault.title: Floor 4 - Blood Vault
floor4_blood_vault.text: A red key hangs from a chain of stamped medical tags. Each tag has a competitor number. Some are crossed out. Yours has been left blank.

choices.text: Claim the Blood Vault Key
Leave the Blood Vault

floor4_signal_entry.title: Floor 4 - Signal Wing Entrance
floor4_signal_entry.text: The Signal Wing does not have walls so much as permissions. Screens show earlier floors from impossible angles. Someone has clipped your best moments into sponsor bait.

choices.text: Trace the broadcast source
Rush the signal corridor

floor4_signal_puzzle.title: Floor 4 - Signal Patch
floor4_signal_puzzle.text: Sponsor Pressure: a cracked broadcast line lets you patch the Champion feed. The patch will weaken its armor routine, but the relay burns feedback through your nervous system.

choices.text: Accept Sponsor Pressure - patch the Champion feed
Solve only the safe part of the broadcast puzzle

floor4_signal_vault.title: Floor 4 - Signal Vault
floor4_signal_vault.text: A key made of blue static waits inside a soundless server rack. It flickers between your hand and the screen, then decides both are real enough.

choices.text: Claim the Signal Vault Key
Leave the Signal Vault

floor4_boss_gate.title: Floor 4 - Sponsor Gate
floor4_boss_gate.text: Three key slots ring the gate. Gold wants proof of greed. Blood wants proof of survival. Signal wants proof that you can see the hook before it pulls you.

choices.text: Return to the sponsor relay
Re-enter the Gold Wing
Re-enter the Blood Wing
Re-enter the Signal Wing
Slot all three Vault Keys and challenge the Champion

floor4_boss.title: Floor 4 - The Sponsor's Champion
floor4_boss.text: The arena is a glass bowl suspended in broadcast light. The Sponsor's Champion steps out wearing too many logos and not enough fear. Every sponsor contract you bent now pulls against them.

combat.name: The Sponsor's Champion
combat.intro: The Champion raises one hand. The sponsors raise the odds.
combat.victoryText: The Champion falls quiet. For the first time, the broadcast has no prepared line.

floor4_clear_room.title: Floor 4 Clear - Broadcast Cut
floor4_clear_room.text:
The Sponsor Vault goes dark one logo at a time. Vale removes the silver mask and looks suddenly tired. Above the arena, the sponsors keep bidding, but the Overseers interrupt the feed before the numbers finish climbing.

A service hatch opens under the dead broadcast board. The sign reads: FLOOR 5 ACCESS PENDING. Beneath it, a second line appears for half a second: OVERSEERS ONLY.

For the first time, the Sponsors are not the only ones watching you.

choices.text: Step into the Overseer hatch. [FLOOR 4 COMPLETE]

floor5_service_dock.title: Floor 5 - Overseer Service Dock
floor5_service_dock.text: The Overseer Service Dock is a safe room carved behind the broadcast walls: bed alcoves, repair lights, sealed vending drawers, and a silent clerk made of brass stamps. A wall display reads Protocol Clearances 0/4. The clerk will not bargain, but it will sell supplies and point to four protocol doors. Every door tests a different rule in the dungeon engine.

choices.text: Rest in the service bed
Buy a Large Potion from the service drawer - 45 gold
Enter the Combat Protocol chamber
Enter the Memory Protocol chamber
Enter the Debt Protocol chamber
Enter the Identity Protocol chamber
Approach the Rulekeeper gate

floor5_combat_protocol.title: Floor 5 - Combat Protocol
floor5_combat_protocol.text: The Combat Protocol lists every fight you have survived and marks the messy parts in red. Complying gives you a fair arena. Overriding scars the rule before the Rulekeeper can use it.

choices.text: Comply with the Combat Protocol
Override the Combat Protocol and take the backlash

floor5_combat_trial.title: Floor 5 - Combat Trial
floor5_combat_trial.text: A training shell steps out of the wall wearing your stance badly. It fights like a rule trying to become a person.

combat.name: Protocol Duelist
combat.intro: The duelist salutes with a weapon made from red warning text.
combat.victoryText: The shell breaks into neat numbered pieces.

floor5_combat_complete.title: Floor 5 - Combat Clearance
floor5_combat_complete.text: The duel log stamps itself approved. The system admits you survived without becoming what it wanted.

choices.text: Claim the Combat Clearance and return to the dock

floor5_memory_protocol.title: Floor 5 - Memory Protocol
floor5_memory_protocol.text: The Memory Protocol opens with scenes you never chose: routes you skipped, deaths that did not happen, speeches from people you spared. It wants you to agree that the record is cleaner than the truth.

choices.text: Comply with the Memory Protocol
Override the Memory Protocol and keep the contradiction

floor5_memory_trial.title: Floor 5 - Memory Trial
floor5_memory_trial.text: Three false memories hang in glass: a door that was never opened, a contract that signed itself, and a victory without a cost. The true path is the one that still hurts.

choices.text: Name the memory with a cost
Accept the clean record

floor5_memory_complete.title: Floor 5 - Memory Clearance
floor5_memory_complete.text: The archive stutters, then stamps your version beside the official one. For once, both are allowed to exist.

choices.text: Claim the Memory Clearance and return to the dock

floor5_debt_protocol.title: Floor 5 - Debt Protocol
floor5_debt_protocol.text: The Debt Protocol is a counting house for damage, gold, favors, and fear. It claims every borrowed edge must be paid back with interest.

choices.text: Comply with the Debt Protocol
Override the Debt Protocol and erase a line of interest

floor5_debt_trial.title: Floor 5 - Debt Trial
floor5_debt_trial.text: An iron ledger asks for payment in three currencies. Gold is easiest. Blood is fastest. Refusal costs both but earns respect from the clerk watching behind the wall.

choices.text: Pay the ledger in gold
Pay the ledger in blood
Refuse the ledger and endure the audit

floor5_debt_complete.title: Floor 5 - Debt Clearance
floor5_debt_complete.text: The ledger closes with a sound like a door choosing not to lock.

choices.text: Claim the Debt Clearance and return to the dock

floor5_identity_protocol.title: Floor 5 - Identity Protocol
floor5_identity_protocol.text: The Identity Protocol offers a mirror with preset names: Prisoner, Product, Asset, Failure, Champion. None of them fit without cutting something off.

choices.text: Comply with the Identity Protocol
Override the Identity Protocol and reject the labels

floor5_identity_trial.title: Floor 5 - Identity Trial
floor5_identity_trial.text: Your reflection climbs out holding the version of you the system would prefer: simpler, crueler, easier to file.

combat.name: Filed Reflection
combat.intro: The reflection smiles with your mouth and the Overseer signature behind its teeth.
combat.victoryText: The mirror breaks, but your shape stays yours.

floor5_identity_complete.title: Floor 5 - Identity Clearance
floor5_identity_complete.text: The mirror stamps no name at all. The blank space feels more honest than a title.

choices.text: Claim the Identity Clearance and return to the dock

floor5_boss_gate.title: Floor 5 - Rulekeeper Gate
floor5_boss_gate.text: Four brass slots wait in the last door. Combat, Memory, Debt, Identity. The Rulekeeper will only answer a complete file.

choices.text: Return to the service dock
Open the Rulekeeper door with all four Protocol Clearances

floor5_boss.title: Floor 5 - The Rulekeeper
floor5_boss.text: The Rulekeeper unfolds from the ceiling as a judge, clerk, engine, and executioner sharing one body. Every override sigil you stole now burns inside its rulebook.

combat.name: The Rulekeeper
combat.intro: The Rulekeeper stamps the air. The room tries to make your choices illegal.
combat.victoryText: The last stamp falls without ink. The rulebook keeps turning pages, but none of them can find your name.

floor5_clear_room.title: Floor 5 Clear - Rulebook Empty
floor5_clear_room.text: The Rulekeeper Core cools in your hand. The service dock lights switch from command white to emergency green, and a wall you thought was load-bearing slides aside. Beyond it is not another cell, market, vault, or protocol. It is weather. Floor 6 waits outside the system, where the dungeon has fewer rules and more teeth.

choices.text: Step beyond the system. [FLOOR 5 COMPLETE]

floor6_weather_gap.title: Floor 6 - The Weather Gap
floor6_weather_gap.text: The Weather Gap is the first safe place outside the system, though safe is only half true. Rain falls upward, the horizon loads in pieces, and the dungeon walls end like a sentence cut short. A cracked sign reads Anchor Shards 0/3. Stabilize Glass Rain Field, Rooted Static, and Nameless Road before the outside notices you completely.

choices.text: Rest under the broken sky
Scavenge the crash kit for a Large Potion
Enter the Glass Rain Field
Enter Rooted Static
Walk the Nameless Road
Approach the Anchor gate

floor6_glass_field.title: Floor 6 - Glass Rain Field
floor6_glass_field.text: Glass rain hangs in the air, each shard reflecting a different possible room. Normal steps make the field behave. Fracture steps make it remember that it was never built for feet.

choices.text: Take the marked path through the glass field
Touch the fracture in the glass rain and take its anomaly

floor6_glass_rain.title: Floor 6 - Hanging Rain
floor6_glass_rain.text: The rain will cut anything moving in a straight line. The only safe route is a crooked answer: forward, aside, wait, forward again.

choices.text: cross the glass rain by moving crooked
Sprint through the rain before it chooses a direction

floor6_glass_anchor.title: Floor 6 - Glass Anchor
floor6_glass_anchor.text: A shard of clear sky sits in a crater. When you lift it, the glass rain remembers gravity for a few seconds.

choices.text: Claim the Glass Anchor Shard and return to the Weather Gap

floor6_rooted_static.title: Floor 6 - Rooted Static
floor6_rooted_static.text: Trees grow from dead signal. Their leaves hiss with voices from every floor below. The normal path keeps distance. The fracture path lets the static root in your shadow.

choices.text: Circle the static grove at a distance
Break the fracture root and take its anomaly

floor6_static_grove.title: Floor 6 - Static Grove
floor6_static_grove.text: A thing wearing bark and broken announcements crawls out of the rooted static. It repeats your old objective tracker in a voice that hates you.

combat.name: Static Rootbound
combat.intro: The grove says your name in the wrong order.
combat.victoryText: The static drops into the soil and stays quiet.

floor6_root_anchor.title: Floor 6 - Root Anchor
floor6_root_anchor.text: The grove leaves one root behind, braided around a piece of quiet. It steadies the ground when you take it.

choices.text: Claim the Root Anchor Shard and return to the Weather Gap

floor6_nameless_road.title: Floor 6 - Nameless Road
floor6_nameless_road.text: The road has no signs because signs are a kind of permission. It tries to remove names from your map, your items, and eventually you. The fracture ahead is shaped like a missing word.

choices.text: Follow the road without naming it
Break the nameless fracture and take its anomaly

floor6_road_mile.title: Floor 6 - The Mile That Repeats
floor6_road_mile.text: You pass the same stone three times. Each time it has a different name scratched into it. The road wants you to accept one. The trick is to keep walking until the name returns to you instead.

choices.text: walk until the name returns
Carve a temporary name into the stone

floor6_road_anchor.title: Floor 6 - Road Anchor
floor6_road_anchor.text: The road gives up a black stone with your footprint already in it. It is heavier than distance should be.

choices.text: Claim the Road Anchor Shard and return to the Weather Gap

floor6_boss_gate.title: Floor 6 - Anchor Gate
floor6_boss_gate.text: Three Anchor Shards turn in the air without touching anything. Behind them, the outside presses its face against the gap in the world.

choices.text: Return to the Weather Gap
Open the outside gate with all three Anchor Shards

floor6_boss.title: Floor 6 - The Outside Thing
floor6_boss.text: The Outside Thing arrives without entering. It is weather, hunger, road, root, reflection, and something that has never heard of floors. Your Anomaly Marks make parts of it disagree with itself.

combat.name: The Outside Thing
combat.intro: The outside leans in. The room forgets which way damage is supposed to travel.
combat.victoryText: The Outside Thing folds backward into weather. The gap remains, but now it knows your shape.

floor6_clear_room.title: Floor 6 Clear - First Free Weather
floor6_clear_room.text: The Outside Heart beats once and the Weather Gap becomes a doorway instead of a wound. Behind you, the dungeon still counts floors. Ahead, Floor 7 is the first free zone, a place not yet named by Overseers, Sponsors, markets, or rules.

choices.text: Step into the first free zone. [FLOOR 6 COMPLETE]

floor7_freecamp.title: Floor 7 - Freecamp
floor7_freecamp.text: Freecamp is the First Free Zone: canvas roofs, cooking smoke, fence posts, arguments, children sleeping under borrowed armor, and no Overseer signs anywhere. The settlement will not open the boss trail until you earn Trust Bonds 0/4 from the Foragers, Scouts, Healers, and Builders.

choices.text: Rest beside the Freecamp cookfire
Trade camp stories for a Large Potion
Help the Foragers at the living orchard
Join the Scouts on the no-rule ridge
Assist the Healers in the weather tents
Work with the Builders on the wall
Approach the Council Fire

floor7_forager_orchard.title: Floor 7 - Forager Orchard
floor7_forager_orchard.text: The Foragers found trees growing fruit shaped like closed fists. Food means survival, but the orchard twitches when anyone takes too much.

choices.text: Take only what Freecamp can eat tonight
share the first safe fruit with the hungry kids and earn a forager favor

floor7_living_orchard.title: Floor 7 - Living Orchard
floor7_living_orchard.text: The orchard opens paths only when you harvest in rhythm with the roots. Too quick and it bites. Too slow and the fruit spoils in your hand.

choices.text: harvest the living orchard in root rhythm
Cut a fast basket before the branches close

floor7_forager_bond.title: Floor 7 - Forager Trust
floor7_forager_bond.text: The Foragers count the baskets, then count the people you fed first. They nod as if that math matters more.

choices.text: Claim the Forager Trust Bond and return to Freecamp

floor7_scout_ridge.title: Floor 7 - Scout Ridge
floor7_scout_ridge.text: The Scouts climb a ridge where maps refuse to stay drawn. From here, Freecamp looks small enough to lose and stubborn enough to matter.

choices.text: Follow the scout markers quietly
stand watch for the slowest scout and earn a scout favor

floor7_no_rule_ridge.title: Floor 7 - No-Rule Ridge
floor7_no_rule_ridge.text: The ridge has no north. The Scouts ask you to map it anyway, not because the map will be perfect, but because people walk braver when someone tried.

choices.text: map the no-rule ridge by landmarks, not directions
Mark a faster route through unstable ground

floor7_scout_bond.title: Floor 7 - Scout Trust
floor7_scout_bond.text: The Scouts pin your rough map beside their own. It is ugly, useful, and already saving arguments.

choices.text: Claim the Scout Trust Bond and return to Freecamp

floor7_healer_tents.title: Floor 7 - Healer Tents
floor7_healer_tents.text: The Healers work under stitched tarps while free weather crawls through bandages. They need hands, not speeches.

choices.text: Sort medicine and keep quiet
help carry the injured through the worst gust and earn a healer favor

floor7_weather_sick.title: Floor 7 - Weather Sick Ward
floor7_weather_sick.text: The patients are sick with places they briefly stood in: glass rain in the lungs, static in the blood, road dust under the skin.

choices.text: stabilize the weather sick one breath at a time
Burn scarce supplies to save time

floor7_healer_bond.title: Floor 7 - Healer Trust
floor7_healer_bond.text: One patient wakes and asks if Freecamp is still there. The Healers look at you when they answer yes.

choices.text: Claim the Healer Trust Bond and return to Freecamp

floor7_builder_wall.title: Floor 7 - Builder Wall
floor7_builder_wall.text: The Builders are raising a wall from wrecked doors, boss bones, and things nobody wants to explain. It is not pretty. It is standing.

choices.text: Haul braces to the weak side
stand on the wall while the others reinforce it and earn a builder favor

floor7_defense_line.title: Floor 7 - Defense Line
floor7_defense_line.text: A Claimant outrider tests the new wall with hooks and old ownership papers. The Builders shout advice that sounds a lot like courage.

combat.name: Claimant Outrider
combat.intro: The outrider points at Freecamp like it has already bought the place.
combat.victoryText: The wall holds. The ownership papers do not.

floor7_builder_bond.title: Floor 7 - Builder Trust
floor7_builder_bond.text: The Builders carve your mark into a brace where only they will see it. That is how they say thank you.

choices.text: Claim the Builder Trust Bond and return to Freecamp

floor7_council_fire.title: Floor 7 - Council Fire
floor7_council_fire.text: The Council Fire is not a throne. It is four circles of people disagreeing honestly. If every Trust Bond is present, they open the boss trail together.

choices.text: Return to Freecamp
Open the boss trail with all four Trust Bonds

floor7_boss.title: Floor 7 - The Claimant
floor7_boss.text: The Claimant arrives with banners, ledgers, and a smile polished by conquest. It says freedom is only land nobody stronger has named yet. Freecamp answers from behind you.

combat.name: The Claimant
combat.intro: The Claimant plants a flag where your shadow falls.
combat.victoryText: The flag comes down. Freecamp does not cheer at first. It listens to the silence and realizes it is still free.

floor7_clear_room.title: Floor 7 Clear - Freecamp Holds
floor7_clear_room.text: Freecamp raises its banner where the Claimant tried to plant one. Nobody agrees what freedom should become next, which is how you know it survived. Beyond the settlement, Floor 8 waits in the wider wild, past the first free zone and into country no one has defended yet.

choices.text: Walk beyond Freecamp. [FLOOR 7 COMPLETE]

floor8_trailhead_camp.title: Floor 8 - Trailhead Camp
floor8_trailhead_camp.text: Trailhead Camp is a ring of lanterns nailed to dead trees. The hunters here speak softly because the Pale Stalker learns voices. A carved board reads: Hunt Traps 0/4. Set Scent, Snare, Echo, and Sight before you step into the killing ground.

choices.text: Rest in the canvas bed before the hunt.
Buy a large potion from the trail trader. (55 gold)
Take the Scent Trail.
Walk to the Bone Snare field.
Enter the Echo Blind.
Climb toward the Moon Blind.
Approach the Killing Ground.

floor8_scent_trail.title: Floor 8 - Scent Trail
floor8_scent_trail.text: The trail is painted in old musk, crushed mint, and hunter ash. Claw marks stop at every place a frightened person would hide.

choices.text: bait yourself with hunter ash and walk first.
Follow the prepared scent line carefully.

floor8_marked_brush.title: Floor 8 - Marked Brush
floor8_marked_brush.text: Ribbons of hide hang from thorn branches. Each strip carries a different lie about where prey has gone.

choices.text: read the marked brush and spoil the false trail.
Move through the brush by instinct.

floor8_scent_trap.title: Floor 8 - Scent Trap
floor8_scent_trap.text: A copper basin waits under a split pine. Once lit, it will drag the Stalker by memory instead of hunger.

choices.text: Set the Scent Trap and return to camp.
Return to Trailhead Camp.

floor8_bone_snare.title: Floor 8 - Bone Snare Field
floor8_bone_snare.text: The ground is stitched with pale ribs. Hunters left the bones standing upright so anything charging blind breaks itself on the pattern.

choices.text: offer fresh blood to wake the snare pattern.
Step between the ribs and keep your blood.

floor8_old_kill_site.title: Floor 8 - Old Kill Site
floor8_old_kill_site.text: A circle of crushed helmets marks where the Pale Stalker learned that armor makes a lovely sound when folded.

choices.text: bind the old kill site with wire and prayer.
Skirt the kill site and keep moving.

floor8_snare_trap.title: Floor 8 - Snare Trap
floor8_snare_trap.text: Braided wire vanishes under leaves and bone dust. It will not kill the Stalker. It only needs to teach the thing one moment of stillness.

choices.text: Set the Snare Trap and return to camp.
Return to Trailhead Camp.

floor8_echo_blind.title: Floor 8 - Echo Blind
floor8_echo_blind.text: A blind of black cloth hangs over a canyon mouth. Inside, every breath returns late, wearing teeth.

choices.text: risk a shout and make the canyon answer you.
Cross the blind in silence.

floor8_canyon_echo.title: Floor 8 - Canyon Echo
floor8_canyon_echo.text: The canyon keeps repeating footsteps that have not happened yet. Somewhere below, something repeats yours perfectly.

choices.text: break the canyon echo with a cracked bell.
Let the echo fade on its own.

floor8_echo_trap.title: Floor 8 - Echo Trap
floor8_echo_trap.text: Three bells hang in a triangle. When rung together, they make a silence sharp enough to cut pursuit.

choices.text: Set the Echo Trap and return to camp.
Return to Trailhead Camp.

floor8_moon_blind.title: Floor 8 - Moon Blind
floor8_moon_blind.text: Moonlight falls here in broken panels, bright enough to reveal skin and dark enough to hide claws.

choices.text: risk: stand in broken moonlight until the Stalker sees you.
Keep to the shadow line.

floor8_broken_moonlight.title: Floor 8 - Broken Moonlight
floor8_broken_moonlight.text: A moonlit decoy peels itself from your outline and comes at you with your own impatience.

combat.name: Moonlit Decoy
combat.intro: The decoy smiles with your mouth.
combat.victoryText: The false outline tears apart and leaves the Sight Trap components behind.

floor8_sight_trap.title: Floor 8 - Sight Trap
floor8_sight_trap.text: Mirrored teeth click into a circle. When the Stalker crosses it, every shadow will point at the real body.

choices.text: Set the Sight Trap and return to camp.
Return to Trailhead Camp.

floor8_killing_ground.title: Floor 8 - Killing Ground
floor8_killing_ground.text: The trees stop at a perfect circle. The Pale Stalker has killed here often enough that even the soil knows to stay flat.

choices.text: Return to Trailhead Camp.
Set all four Hunt Traps and call the Pale Stalker.

floor8_boss.title: Floor 8 - The Pale Stalker
floor8_boss.text: The Pale Stalker enters without sound. It is too long, too still, and too familiar with fear. The four Hunt Traps wake around it one by one.

combat.name: The Pale Stalker
combat.intro: The Pale Stalker lowers its antlered skull and chooses the sound of your heartbeat.
combat.victoryText: The Pale Stalker falls into every trap at once. When it stops moving, the wild remembers how to breathe.

floor8_clear_room.title: Floor 8 Clear - Hide Under Stars
floor8_clear_room.text: The hunters hang the Pale Stalker hide over the trailhead fire. Past it, Floor 9 opens into deeper wilderness where old power moves under the roots and even the market maps go blank.

choices.text: Follow the old power deeper. [FLOOR 8 COMPLETE]

floor9_root_shrine.title: Floor 9 - Root Cathedral Shrine
floor9_root_shrine.text: The Root Cathedral is not built. It grew around a buried altar and decided to become holy. Old power moves under the bark like breath. A root-carved tablet reads: Ancient Roots 0/3. Awaken Glass, Blood, and Ash before the Buried Saint opens its eyes.

choices.text: Rest beside the moss altar.
Buy a large potion from the root pilgrim. (60 gold)
Enter the Glass Root path.
Enter the Blood Root path.
Enter the Ash Root path.
Approach the Saint Gate.

floor9_glass_root_path.title: Floor 9 - Glass Root Path
floor9_glass_root_path.text: Glass roots arch overhead, reflecting versions of you that made cleaner choices. They watch without blinking.

choices.text: risk the old power and let the glass remember you.
Walk the reflections without touching them.

floor9_mirror_grove.title: Floor 9 - Mirror Grove
floor9_mirror_grove.text: Every tree here reflects a different exit. Only one reflection shows dirt under your boots.

choices.text: solve the mirror grove by following the dirty reflection.
Close your eyes and walk by root pressure.

floor9_glass_root_heart.title: Floor 9 - Glass Root Heart
